Title: Assamites win storyline in Elko, Nevada!

Messages.Author: Brian Iverson
Messages.Body:
Sorry for the delay in getting this long report to the newsgroup.
Better late than never.

Unofficial Report for Storyline Elko – September 20, 2003
Official report already sent to Robert and Robyn.

9 Methuselah's participated and the final rankings were:

1. Assamites – Matt Leahy
2. Malkavians – Misty Martin
3. Tzimisce/Lambach – Brian Iverson
4. Ventrue – Warner Glenn
5. Giovanni – Eric Stott
6. Nosferatu – Jeremiah Moore
7. Brujah – Cody Shook
8. Tremere – Jeremy Killion
9. Harbingers – RJ Santos

A long report of the final round follows after this, the winning deck,

Deck Name: Assamites
Created By: Matt Leahy
Description: Rush and torp then eat with Smudge or Tariq.

Crypt: (13 cards, Min: 7, Max: 28, Avg: 4.31)
---------------------------------------------
1 Abd al-Rashid CEL obf QUI 5, Assamite
1 Ali Kar obf qui 3, Assamite
1 Anwar cel obf qui 4, Assamite
1 Badr al-Budur cel dom OBF qui 5, Assamite
1 Fatima al-Faqadi aus CEL for OBF QUI 8, Assamite
1 Harika Guljan QUI 3, Assamite
1 Jalal Sayad CEL pot QUI 6, Assamite
1 Kanya Akhtar cel 2, Assamite
1 Parmenides CEL qui 4, Assamite
2 Smudge the Ignored none 1, Caitiff
2 Tariq AUS cel FOR OBF QUI 7, Assamite

Library: (90 cards)
-------------------
Master (23 cards)
3 Blood Doll
3 Celerity
1 Haven Uncovered
2 Information Highway
4 Minion Tap
1 Mob Connections
1 Path of Blood, The
3 Quietus
1 Secret Horde
1 Short-Term Investment
2 Tension in the Ranks
1 Underworld Hunting Ground

Action (18 cards)
18 Bum's Rush

Combat (42 cards)
1 Acrobatics
1 Disease
3 Flash
1 Infernal Pursuit
8 Lucky Blow
4 Psyche!
7 Stutter-Step
10 Taste of Death
1 Taste of Vitae
5 Thin Blood
1 Vascular Explosion

Equipment (7 cards)
2 Bang Nakh - Tiger's Claws
1 Gas-Powered Chainsaw
1 Ivory Bow
1 Kali's Fang
2 Sengir Dagger

The final round was recorded by Jeremiah Moore. Some of the words have
been changed so as not to offend the easily offended. Seating was
Giovanni-Assamite-Ventrue-Tzimisce-Malkavian. Not everything was
recorded, only the interesting stuff. See the very end for a quick
report of play.

Lucinde appears.
Lambach appears.

Lambach ‘reads the winds' and calls baloney on Lucinde who was trying
to become a Camarilla Exemplary. Lam tries to stomp a mudhole in Luci,
but she ‘rolls with the punches' and bitch slaps Lam for one damage.

Lambach summons an ‘army of rats' and cries, "Go forth my minions and
feast on her innards!"

Assamites refrain from killing Luci. (Assamites are now sucking up to
Ventrue as lapdogs)

Lambach ‘reads the winds' and blocks Lucinde trying to ‘govern the
unaligned.' Yet again Lam tries to stomp a mudhole in Luci but she is
just too ‘Majestic.' Lambach snaps out of it, ‘reads the winds' and
again blocks Lucinda who is now trying to call for a ‘parody shift.'
Luci once again ‘rolls with the punches' and avoids the mudhole
stomping of Lam.

Lambach's rats bleed the Malks, then he uses his ‘fiendish tongue' to
lick the blood from the wound. Lucinde vows vengeance on Lam and
shouts, "The Kiss of Ra will bringith the smackith down!" (Ventrue
sticking up for their Malk friends)

Lucinde throws Wilhelm to the Assamites as a tribute to them for not
rolling her like a tumbleweed. (Wilhelm actually was blocking a rush
on Lucinde)
Wilhelm escapes Fatima by using Luci's technique of ‘rolling with the
punches.'

Smudge, being the opportunist that he is, tries his luck by ‘bum
rushing' Wil after he ran from Fatima, but Wil was just to damn
‘majestic' for Smudge.
Wilhelm makes a ‘consanguinous boon' for the Assamites to keep them
off of him.

Lucinde bleeds the shit out of the Tzimisce. "I'm your huckleberry!"

Lambach summons a ‘war ghoul' to fight at his side.

Fatima tells Smudge to ‘kill the war ghoul.' Smudge replies in a whiny
voice, "Screw you, get it yourself!" Fatima shrugs and tries to rush
the war ghoul but Lam says, "I don't think so bitch! Combat
ensues…much brawling and blood was spilled. When the dust settles,
Fatima still stands…but for how long?

Luci calls for a ‘parody shift' but Dragos wakes from a ‘special
report' and blocks. Luci gives Dragos the ‘Kiss of Ra'….eww…and Dragos
goes to torpor.
The war ghoul, confused at having no masters, rampages and rolls over
Lucinde. The mudhole has been stomped! Luci is torped. …good ghoulie…

Dragos gets out of torpor.

The Giovanni, (having up to this time done nothing except be
brutalized by the Assamites), send Rudolpho to diablerize Lambach.
Dragos ‘reads the winds' like superfly TNT! Moving to long range with
‘chiropteran marauder' they shout naughty words at each other and go
home.

Tariq tries to eat Luci. Wilhelm, being the slave monkey that he is,
throws himself in the way and is all ‘majestic' and stuff. Smudge,
being the lowly opportunist that he is, sneaks along the path of death
created by the war ghoul and his Assamite masters, and eats Lucinde!

Dragos rescues Lambach.

Once Lambach wakes and is told of the nasty attempt upon him by
Rudolpho, he sends the war ghoul on a mission. The war ghoul has a
light snack. War ghoul number two, (having appeared sometime back),
rolls down the buffet line and poor ol' Wil was the shrimp cocktail.
Wilhelm, well you know, he is just to damn MAJESTIC, and the war ghoul
walks on by.

Abd al-Rashid and Lambach play patty cake when Wilhelm deflects a
bleed by Abd.
The Assamites, try as they might, could not pull themselves from under
the Ventrue boot, cry a little bit and go kill a Giovanni. Feeling a
little better about themselves, ‘bums rush' Wilhelm and play patty
cake once again. Thinking they have the Ventrue, they attempt another
bleed only to have Wil send them masterfully to the Tzimisce, who do
bleed.

The Assamites finally kill the Ventrue and there was much rejoicing!!

The Tzimisce war ghouls turn on the Assamites and make oreos out of
them. Assamites begin much thrashing and whining.

In the end, the Assamites, Malkavians, and the Tzimisce have a nice
cup of tea, play patty cake, and go home.

Here is a quick rendition of the play.
Assamites and Tzimisce, knowing the only winners in a fight between
them would be the others, more or less leave each other alone.
The Assamites quickly thrash the Giovanni, then the Malkavians until
they are helpless.
Between the rushes from their Assamite predator, and the wakes from
their Tzimisce prey, the Ventrue are finally ousted.
The Tzimisce war ghouls then quickly torp all the Assamites, thus
making the Assamite player totally helpless. In the meantime, the
Malks, having one vampire with a ‘secure haven' manage to finish off
the Giovanni.
As the Tzimisce are gearing up to bleed out the Malks, time runs out.

Assamites 1.5 VP
Malkavians 1.5VP
Tzimisce-Lambach 0.5 VP

Assamites, having been saved by the bell, win the final round by
having the most game wins going into the finals.

There ya have it,
Brian Iverson
Prince of Elko

The Basic premise to the deck is rush the vampires early and often,
using the tastes of death to send big vampires to torpor, then eat
them with smudge. If smudge survives(which he usually does for fear of
peoples other voters being the next rushed_ he gets +1 hand damage
plus he now has a discpline card(which is always quietus for the taste
of deaths)the stutters steps are very useful if the bums rush IS
blocked as it keeps you from taking any nasty hand damage from your
opponent (and there is almost always another bums rush on the way)
not to mention one hand damage still hurts when its ag damage(ie with
sengir dagger) or adds up quickly with Bahk Nahgsor a chainsaw and
lucky blow(4 total damage and thats without a press or additional
strikes)not to mention the damage smudge now does with something like
bahk naghh or a gas powered chainsaw.(4-5 per hit due ot his damage
bonus from diablre along with a lucky blow)While the master card pool
is a bit high I find that is a weakness in most of my decks as i am
afraid to not have enough master cards and unfortunately with this
deck it is very hard to gain alot of pool back without them.I didnt
notice alot of stalling form the masters but thats mainly due to im
drawing alot of cards during combat anyway. As far as Ali Kar
(DAMMIT!!) He was a last minute addition and didt notice thats smudge
was series 1(i thought he was 2)All in all i feel the deck works well
as you tend to get out vampires fast and if they dont block your
rushes no one else gets vampires out at all. In all three rounds of
the tournament here, i found it easy to cripple both my predator and
prey. and the threat of a rush can do wonders when all an opponent has
is one high capacity vampire. Its weaknesses are blood pool gain and
keeeping the vampires stocked on blood I would like to have some more
taste of vitae so when i did stutter step i could refill my
vampire(and then refill my pool thru minion tapbut unfortunately for
some starnge reason i dont own any more then one)I DID find it
surprising that smudge rarely was burned from blood hunts( i assume it
was the fear of where my next rush would go or in some cases I was
helpin someone out by hurting their predator and they would vote
against the hunt)but it wasnt unheard of by the end of a round to have
smudge up to 5 capacity with master celerity and master quietus along
with his 2 hand damage and some bahk nahgs he became a force to reckon
with. and when he did fail Tariq was there to eat the victim in his
place.Fatima is great for getting weapons out as i have her rush, pull
a weapon, fight the battle then have another vampire take the weapon
from her.soon i have several small vampire out who are all armed to
the teeth which makes even close range a risky propisition. Stealth
bleed decks are a big fear to this deck as i dont carry any intercept
. During the tournament any stealth bleed decks were the first people
hit with rushes. I would cripple them just enough where all they could
do was attempt to hold off their prey(had this backlash me in the
final as my malk opponent got out a secured haven out on her last
vampire thus stopping my rushes)My next target was always voters, if
by this time i havent talked them into casting votes for me by that
is.I tend to leave combat deck for last unless they happen to be my
predator as they tend not to bleed alot and if i have crippled their
prey they usually sit there bleeding for one for several rounds as
their hand is jammed with combat cards. in the finals my second
mistake was holding off to long on the Lambach Deck as by the time it
came to him and I he had two war ghouls out and was intercepting like
mad. In hindsight I should have pressed my attack on him when the
first war ghoul was out and his two vampires were in torpor. A mistake
i will not forget for next time. If anyone has
some suggestions for this deck plz let me know as I am always open to
advice and thanks for taking a look at it

Well ya learn something new everyday I always say. You see, Matt is
just a 'cheating ass roach'. No wonder he wins so often! Actually,
Matt is a very good player. Our local group in Elko, while maybe not
the best at knowing all the rules of VTES, does a pretty good job at
trying to learn them. I place the blame on myself for not knowing the
complete definition of 'hand-strike', as follows:

Hand Strike: any non-ranged, non-weapon strike that deals damage based
on the striking minion's strength, or any minion's non-ranged
damage-dealing innate strike. [LSJ 19970224]

I just looked this up in the errata, and now I know. We have
apparantly been using Stutter-step incorrectly with weapons. Just
reading the first part of Stutter-step, see below, you get a dodge and
then strike for strength damage.

Stutter-Step:
[cel] Strike: dodge. [CEL] Strike: dodge and inflict strength damage.
This damage may be modified by effects that modify hand damage. This
is both a hand strike and a dodge. It cannot be used if dodges are
restricted Only usable at close range. Not usable as an additional
strike, and this vampire cannot use any additional strikes this round.

As far as Matt's deck is concerned, Smudge could still be doing 3
damage with Stutter-Step. (+1 strength from diablerie and Lucky Blow)
Without Stutter-Step, he could do 3 agg with Sengir or 5 damage with
Gas-powered chainsaw or Bang Nakh. Correct? Not bad for a weenie.

As for the Ali Kar illegal crypt, no one noticed that either, and like
Matt said, he had only recently added it to his deck. I don't even
remember seeing Ali Kar show up during the tournament.

I hope this does not alter the results of our Storyline. No
intentional cheating was going on, only some misinterpretation of the
rules, and errors on our part. All in all, we had a great time, and it
was a fun event. Jeremiah had a lot of fun keeping track of the final
round events.



Messages.Author: David Cherryholmes
Messages.Body:
"Brian Iverson" <Iverso...@citlink.net> wrote in message

> Stutter-Step:
> [cel] Strike: dodge. [CEL] Strike: dodge and inflict strength damage.
> This damage may be modified by effects that modify hand damage. This
> is both a hand strike and a dodge. It cannot be used if dodges are
> restricted Only usable at close range. Not usable as an additional
> strike, and this vampire cannot use any additional strikes this round.

> Without Stutter-Step, he could do 3 agg with Sengir or 5 damage with
> Gas-powered chainsaw or Bang Nakh. Correct? Not bad for a weenie.

Wrong. Lucky Blow is still a *strike*. Stutterstep doesn't allow for the
playing of any more *strike* cards, in addition to its other limitations.
The easiest example of the "modify hand damage" clause is a Torn Signpost.
